questions.prompt: Describe the cerebral cortex: its layers and major functional areas.
questions.original_prompt: Cortex feb1 3
questions.answer: Neocortex has six layers. Frontal lobe contains primary motor and prefrontal areas; parietal lobe primary somatosensory cortex; temporal lobe auditory/language-memory regions; occipital lobe primary visual cortex.

questions.prompt: Describe the motor homunculus and its somatotopic organization.
questions.original_prompt: Muscle homunculus feb1 6
questions.answer: The motor homunculus lies in the precentral gyrus: leg/foot are medial, trunk and upper limb more superolateral, and face/tongue inferolateral. Cortical area reflects precision of motor control rather than body size.

questions.prompt: Describe the brainstem, with particular attention to the medulla oblongata and its nuclei.
questions.original_prompt: Midbrain with particular attention to the medulla oblungata and its nuclei
questions.answer: The brainstem comprises midbrain, pons and medulla. The medulla contains the pyramids, olives, gracile/cuneate nuclei, major ascending/descending tracts, and cranial-nerve nuclei mainly related to IX-XII.
notes: Editorial note: the original prompt conflates midbrain with medulla. Placement follows the supplied brainstem/medulla answer.

questions.original_prompt: position of nuclei in pons;

questions.prompt: Describe the major afferent inputs to the striatum.
questions.original_prompt: Afferents to striatum
questions.answer: Major striatal afferents include glutamatergic corticostriatal and thalamostriatal fibers and dopaminergic nigrostriatal fibers from substantia nigra pars compacta.

questions.prompt: Describe the cerebellum: position, gross anatomy, and functions.
questions.original_prompt: function,position,anatomyx3
questions.answer: The cerebellum lies in the posterior cranial fossa dorsal to pons/medulla. It has vermis plus two hemispheres and anterior, posterior and flocculonodular lobes; it coordinates movement, posture, balance and motor learning.

questions.prompt: Name the layers of the cerebellar cortex from superficial to deep.
questions.original_prompt: cortex + name of its layers (faddy)
questions.answer: Cerebellar cortex has three layers, superficial to deep: molecular layer, Purkinje-cell layer, and granular layer.

questions.prompt: Describe Purkinje cells and their role in cerebellar output.
questions.original_prompt: Purkinje cells: feb 11 ,march 13 ,feb1 5
questions.answer: Purkinje cells are large GABAergic neurons and the sole output neurons of the cerebellar cortex; they inhibit deep cerebellar and vestibular nuclei.

questions.prompt: Name the deep cerebellar nuclei from lateral to medial.
questions.original_prompt: Deep cerebellar nuclei ( faddy)
questions.answer: Deep cerebellar nuclei from lateral to medial are dentate, emboliform, globose and fastigial.

questions.prompt: Describe the principal afferent and efferent pathways of the cerebellum.
questions.original_prompt: Afferent and efferent tracts (faddy)
questions.answer: Cerebellar afferents enter through all three peduncles as mossy or climbing fibers; the middle peduncle is almost entirely afferent. Most deep-nuclear efferents leave through the superior peduncle, with vestibular connections using the inferior peduncle.

questions.prompt: Compare gray and white matter and describe their organization in the spinal cord.
questions.original_prompt: General features of white and gray matter ( Michele)
questions.answer: Gray matter contains neuronal cell bodies, dendrites and synapses; white matter is mainly myelinated axons. In the spinal cord gray matter is central and H-shaped, while white matter is peripheral in posterior, lateral and anterior funiculi.

questions.prompt: Describe a descending motor pathway.
questions.original_prompt: Talk about a descending pathway
questions.answer: Example descending pathway - corticospinal tract: motor cortex -> corona radiata/internal capsule -> cerebral peduncle -> pons -> medullary pyramids -> pyramidal decussation -> lateral corticospinal tract -> spinal motor circuits.

questions.prompt: Describe how conscious sensory information reaches the cerebral cortex.
questions.original_prompt: Describe in general how a sensory information is passed to the cortex
questions.answer: General conscious sensory pathway: receptor -> first-order neuron in a sensory ganglion -> second-order neuron, usually with decussation -> thalamus -> third-order neuron -> primary sensory cortex.

questions.prompt: Compare the fasciculus gracilis and fasciculus cuneatus.
questions.original_prompt: Cuneate and gracilis
questions.answer: Dorsal columns carry fine touch, vibration and conscious proprioception. Fasciculus gracilis carries ipsilateral lower limb/lower trunk; fasciculus cuneatus carries ipsilateral upper trunk/upper limb above T6 before synapsing in the medulla.

questions.prompt: Describe the major ascending sensory pathways.
questions.original_prompt: Ascending pathways
questions.answer: Major ascending systems are dorsal column-medial lemniscus for fine touch/vibration/proprioception, anterolateral/spinothalamic pathways for pain-temperature/crude touch, and spinocerebellar tracts for unconscious proprioception.

questions.prompt: Describe the major descending motor tracts.
questions.original_prompt: Descending tracts feb2
questions.answer: Major descending tracts include corticospinal/corticobulbar for voluntary movement and vestibulospinal, reticulospinal, rubrospinal and tectospinal tracts for posture, tone and reflex orientation.

questions.prompt: Describe the spinothalamic tract: modalities, crossing, and course.
questions.original_prompt: Spinothalamic tract feb 2
questions.answer: The spinothalamic/anterolateral system carries pain and temperature (and crude touch). Second-order neurons cross in the anterior white commissure within about 1-2 spinal levels and ascend contralaterally.

questions.prompt: Describe the fasciculus cuneatus and the sensory information it carries.
questions.original_prompt: Fasciculus cuneatus feb 10
questions.answer: Fasciculus cuneatus carries ipsilateral fine touch, vibration and conscious proprioception from the upper limb and upper trunk above T6 to the cuneate nucleus in the medulla.

questions.prompt: Describe the course of lower spinal nerve roots and the formation of the cauda equina.
questions.original_prompt: Spinal cord

questions.prompt: Describe the locations of major tracts and neuron groups in the spinal cord.
questions.original_prompt: Position of tracts and neurons in spinal cord;
questions.answer: In spinal cord, somatic motor neurons are in the anterior horn, sensory processing mainly in posterior horn, and autonomic preganglionic neurons in lateral horn at relevant levels. Dorsal columns are posterior; corticospinal tracts mainly lateral; anterolateral system lies anterolaterally.

questions.prompt: Describe the facial nerve: fiber types, functions, and targets.
questions.original_prompt: Facial nerve
questions.answer: CN VII is mixed: branchial motor to facial-expression muscles, stapedius, stylohyoid and posterior digastric; taste from anterior two-thirds of tongue; parasympathetic to lacrimal, submandibular and sublingual glands; small somatic sensory component.

questions.prompt: Name the sensory and parasympathetic ganglia associated with the facial nerve.
questions.original_prompt: -ganglia(andrea)
questions.answer: Facial-nerve sensory cell bodies are in the geniculate ganglion. Its parasympathetic fibers synapse in the pterygopalatine ganglion or submandibular ganglion.

questions.prompt: Describe the fiber types carried by the facial nerve and the muscles it innervates.
questions.original_prompt: -types of fibers that it carries and muscles innervated ( Michele)
questions.answer: CN VII carries branchial motor, parasympathetic, taste and small somatic sensory fibers. Motor targets include facial-expression muscles, stapedius, stylohyoid and posterior belly of digastric.

questions.prompt: Describe the vagus nerve and its principal functions.
questions.original_prompt: Vagus : feb 4,march 19
questions.answer: CN X is mixed: motor to palate/pharynx/larynx; parasympathetic to thoracic and abdominal viscera to the left colic flexure; visceral and somatic sensory fibers; taste from the epiglottic region.

questions.prompt: Describe the divisions and principal functions of the trigeminal nerve.

questions.prompt: Describe the sympathetic chain and the routes taken by its preganglionic fibers.
questions.original_prompt: Sympathetic chain feb 13,Andrea
questions.answer: The sympathetic chain is a paired series of paravertebral ganglia from the cervical region to coccyx. Preganglionic neurons arise T1-L2, enter through white rami, and may synapse locally, ascend/descend, or pass as splanchnic nerves.

questions.prompt: Describe parasympathetic outflow, fiber lengths, neurotransmitters, and receptors.
questions.original_prompt: Parasympathetic fibers :feb 14,march 21
questions.answer: Parasympathetic outflow is craniosacral (CN III, VII, IX, X and S2-S4). Long preganglionic fibers release acetylcholine onto nicotinic receptors; short postganglionic fibers release acetylcholine onto muscarinic receptors.

questions.prompt: Compare autonomic neurotransmitters and receptors.
questions.original_prompt: Neurotransmitters and receptors (Andrea)
questions.answer: All autonomic preganglionic fibers use acetylcholine at nicotinic receptors. Parasympathetic postganglionics use acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors. Most sympathetic postganglionics use noradrenaline at alpha/beta receptors; sweat glands use acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors.

questions.original_prompt: Vasculature and position of rectum;
questions.answer: Rectum begins near S3 and follows the sacral curve. Arterial supply is superior rectal (IMA), middle rectal (internal iliac) and inferior rectal (internal pudendal); venous drainage has both portal and systemic pathways.

questions.prompt: Indicate the correct statement regarding anatomic relationships of the esophagus:
questions.original_prompt: Indicate the correct statement regarding anatomic relationships of the esophagus:
options: It begins at the level of the thyroid cartilage
In the superior mediastinum, the left brachiocephalic vein constricts the esophagus
It passes through the diaphragm at the T8 level
In the posterior mediastinum, it passes anterior to the aorta before crossing the diaphragm
In the posterior mediastinum, it lies posterior to the right atrium
questions.answer:
D — In the posterior mediastinum, it passes anterior to the aorta before crossing the diaphragm

The oesophagus passes through the diaphragm at T10 and, low in the posterior mediastinum, sweeps anterior to the descending aorta. It lies posterior to the left atrium, not the right atrium.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements concerning liver sinusoids is true?
questions.original_prompt: Which of the following statements concerning liver sinusoids is true?

They are surrounded by a continuous basal lamina
They deliver blood to the central vein
They are lined by non-fenestrated endothelial cells
They perfuse only hepatocytes of the peripheral zone
questions.answer:
C — They deliver blood to the central vein

Hepatic sinusoids carry mixed portal and arterial blood toward the central vein. Their endothelium is fenestrated and they do not have a continuous basal lamina.

The hepatic vein forms the posterior border

The anterior boundary of the epiploic foramen is the hepatoduodenal ligament, which contains the portal triad including the common bile duct.

questions.original_prompt: Which of the following statements best describes the colon?

It is usually invested with peritoneum on all sides

The appendices epiploicae are composed of lymphoid tissue
Its three taenia are formed by the outer longitudinal layer of the muscularis externa
questions.answer:

The three taeniae coli are condensations of the outer longitudinal layer of the muscularis externa. The ascending and descending colon are secondarily, not primarily, retroperitoneal.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the dorsal spinocerebellar tract is accurate?
questions.original_prompt: Which statement about the dorsal spinocerebellar tract is accurate?

It begins at about the level of the second or third lumbar segment
It passes through the inferior cerebellar peduncle
It terminates ipsilaterally in the cerebellar vermis
questions.answer:
E — All of the above

All four statements are standard features of the dorsal spinocerebellar tract: it lies lateral to the lateral corticospinal tract, begins around L2-L3, enters through the inferior cerebellar peduncle, and terminates ipsilaterally in the vermis/paravermis.

questions.prompt: The adrenal gland:
questions.original_prompt: The adrenal gland:
options: Secretes cortisol from the zona glomerulosa of the cortex
Is supplied by branches of the inferior phrenic artery, the renal artery, and the aorta
Is drained by the suprarenal vein reaching the inferior vena cava on the left and the renal vein on the right
questions.answer:
B — Is supplied by branches of the inferior phrenic artery, the renal artery, and the aorta

The suprarenal gland receives superior, middle and inferior suprarenal arteries from the inferior phrenic artery, aorta and renal artery. Cortisol is mainly from zona fasciculata, and venous drainage is right to IVC and left to left renal vein.

questions.original_prompt: Which of the following statements accurately describes relations at the left lung hilum?

The left bronchus passes under the aortic arch

Pulmonary veins are posterior and inferior
The left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops around the left pulmonary artery
questions.answer:
B — The left bronchus passes under the aortic arch

At the left hilum the pulmonary artery lies superior to the bronchus, and the left main bronchus passes beneath the aortic arch. The vagus is posterior to the root and pulmonary veins are mainly anterior/inferior.

It is the attachment site for the round ligament
It communicates with the uterine cavity through the external os
questions.answer:

The cervix forms the lower third of the uterus. The vaginal fornices surround its vaginal part, and the uterine cavity communicates with the cervical canal through the internal os.

questions.prompt: Regarding the ventricular system and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) production, which of the following statements is true?
questions.original_prompt: Regarding the ventricular system and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) production, which of the following statements is true?
options: CSF is exclusively produced in the choroid plexi of the lateral ventricles
CSF passes from the 3rd to the 4th ventricle via the interventricular foramen
The 4th ventricle communicates directly with the subarachnoid space
The total daily production of CSF is approximately 150 ml
CSF is reabsorbed mainly through the arachnoid villi in the inferior sagittal sinus
questions.answer:
C — The 4th ventricle communicates directly with the subarachnoid space

The fourth ventricle communicates directly with the subarachnoid space through the median and lateral apertures. CSF production is roughly 500 mL/day and reabsorption is mainly via arachnoid granulations into dural venous sinuses, especially the superior sagittal sinus.

The spinothalamic system carries pain and temperature. Its ascending fibres are second-order neurons after crossing in the spinal cord.

It crosses the brim of the pelvis at the bifurcation of the common iliac artery
In females it passes under the uterine artery close to the cervix
It enters the bladder at the posterolateral aspect of the trigone
All of the above are correct
questions.answer:

All listed relations are standard: gonadal vessels cross anteriorly, the ureter crosses the pelvic brim near the common iliac bifurcation, passes under the uterine artery near the cervix, and enters the bladder at a posterolateral angle of the trigone.

questions.original_prompt: Which of the following statements concerning the structure of medullary rays in the kidney is true?

They lie at the center of a renal lobule
They contain thin limbs of the loops of Henle

D — They lie at the center of a renal lobule

A renal lobule is centered on a medullary ray. Medullary rays contain straight tubules and collecting ducts extending into the cortex, not renal corpuscles or convoluted tubules.

questions.original_prompt: Which statement about the substantia nigra is accurate?
options: The ventral part consists of pigmented neurons that contain neuromelanin granules
The dorsal part contains mostly GABAergic neurons
It is subdivided into a dorsal pars compacta and a ventral pars reticulata
The ventral part contains mostly dopaminergic neurons
questions.answer:
C — It is subdivided into a dorsal pars compacta and a ventral pars reticulata

The substantia nigra is divided into a dorsal pars compacta and ventral pars reticulata. Pars compacta contains pigmented dopaminergic neurons; pars reticulata is predominantly GABAergic.

sections.title: Most Frequently Tested Topics
paragraphs: Counts describe retained archive occurrences, not future examination probabilities. Repeated exam questions and source versions remain separate occurrences.

sections.title: Pattern of Question Depth
paragraphs: Questions range from identification to structured explanations: name a nucleus, layer, hormone, nerve or artery; describe anatomical relations or a pathway; connect a lesion or vascular injury with its effects.

sections.title: Pattern of Question Style
paragraphs: Common formats include correct-statement MCQs, negative questions, A+B combinations, recall prompts and figure-label matching. Missing figures and incomplete options remain explicitly marked.

sections.title: Suggested Study Priority
paragraphs: Begin with high-count topics, then review connected pathways and organ relations. Practise nerve function, ganglion and target together; trace sensory and motor routes; compare organ coverings, vessels and histology. Review every remaining category. Archive absence does not establish that a topic is unimportant.

sections.title: MCQ Intake Review
paragraphs: Compared all 30 questions in anatomy_mcq_answers.pdf against the original 179 entries. Three equivalent duplicates were skipped (incoming 2, 4, 11); 27 MCQs were added: 7 new tested details and 20 variants with different options or an MCQ form of an existing recall prompt.

Matching considers the tested proposition and full option set, not just topic or correct answer. A+B combinations must be expanded when option order changes. The right-vagus question was retained because its A+B combination includes different statements.
Incoming question 5 has an invisible option E. Its source limitation is preserved. Imported answers are supplied study answers, not independently confirmed official exam keys.
